features.name: 4-Slot Tiered Model Router
features.oneLine: Dynamic turn routing across Guide, Specialist, Vision, and Secure on-device model endpoints.
features.gating: Requires at least one configured LLM endpoint in models.yml
features.whatItIs: Halbert does not route every turn to a single monolithic cloud model. It maintains four dedicated slots: Guide (fast conversational triage), Specialist (complex sysadmin synthesis and code diffing), Vision (image and diagram analysis), and Secure (strictly local, offline on-device inference).
features.howItWorks: Incoming user messages are scored for intent and complexity by intake/pipeline.py. The TierRouter checks available hardware capabilities and configuration before selecting the optimal endpoint pair. If a query touches private credentials or high-tier system configuration, it latches to the Secure slot.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Secure slot must never egress prompts over WAN or public cloud APIs. If a secure endpoint is unavailable, sensitive queries fail closed rather than falling back to cloud models.

subFeatures.name: Secure Offline Slot Latch
subFeatures.oneLine: Hard fail-closed latch ensuring Tier 2 system operations never leak to cloud providers.
subFeatures.whatItIs: A safety boundary that prevents queries with sensitive configuration files or cryptographic keys from being evaluated by remote third-party APIs.
subFeatures.howItWorks: When the classification engine detects sensitive tokens or system file paths, the prompt evaluator locks execution to local loopback endpoints (e.g., Ollama or local Metal/vLLM instances).
subFeatures.limitsAndInvariants: Fails closed: if no local model is available, the turn halts and informs the user rather than silently downgrading to a cloud model.

features.name: ReAct Agent State Machine
features.oneLine: Deterministic finite state machine driving agent planning, tool execution, and reflective verification.
features.whatItIs: The cognitive lifecycle engine that orchestrates turns through formal states: IDLE → PLANNING → EXECUTING → EVALUATING → RESPONDING.
features.howItWorks: Each turn advances through a Haloysius loop. In PLANNING, the model selects tools; in EXECUTING, tools are validated against policy and invoked; in EVALUATING, CRAG checks verify tool outputs before generating the user response.
features.limitsAndInvariants: No infinite tool loops: each turn enforces strict tool call quotas and execution timeouts.

features.name: 3-Panel Host Shell
features.oneLine: Integrated workspace featuring navigation rail, center domain inspection, and right-hand conversation.
features.whatItIs: The primary desktop and browser UI shell for Halbert. Keeps system inventory, active diagnostics, and the conversational agent visible side-by-side without modal context switching.
features.howItWorks: Built in React with keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+D for domain rail, Cmd+J for conversation, Cmd+B for context stage). The conversation maintains contextual awareness of whichever domain page the user currently inspects.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Desktop and mobile responsive: on small screens, gracefully transitions from three side-by-side panels to stacked drawer views.

features.name: Inline Interactive Terminal Tiles
features.oneLine: Live terminal execution tiles embedded directly within chat turns for command transparency.
features.whatItIs: When Halbert proposes running a shell command, the command executes inside an inline terminal tile inside the conversation turn, showing live stdout/stderr and return codes.
features.howItWorks: Streams terminal output via WebSocket from the backend PTY session directly into xterm.js-backed inline tiles, preserving exact terminal formatting and color codes.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Potentially destructive commands require explicit user click approval before execution.

features.name: Pluggable Hardware & OS Scanners
features.oneLine: 26 specialized background probes cataloging system posture across Linux and macOS.
features.whatItIs: An extensible discovery engine that inspects storage volumes, systemd services, thermal sensors, USB devices, GPU accelerators, network interfaces, and installed packages.
features.howItWorks: Scanners run concurrently under an execution budget, parsing native OS sysfs, procfs, systemctl, or macOS ioreg/system_profiler data into strongly-typed Discovery records.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Read-only non-destructive operations: discovery scanners never mutate system state or modify filesystem configuration.

features.name: Finding Attention Ledger & Four Whys
features.oneLine: Unified issue tracking system where every surfaced event carries Why Now, Why Care, Why So, and Why Trust.
features.whatItIs: Replaces raw discovery alerts with curated Findings. Ensures that before Halbert interrupts the user, it can justify why the issue matters and prove its claims with telemetry.
features.howItWorks: Detector sweeps aggregate low-level scanner anomalies. When an anomaly breaches thresholds, a Finding record is generated with four justification fields and queued in the attention ledger.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Zero vanity notifications: respects user-defined quiet hours and the proactivity dial.

features.name: 5-Axis Capability & Consent Model
features.oneLine: Strict multi-dimensional security evaluation: Ceiling, Affordance, OS Grant, Consent, and Runtime.
features.whatItIs: Replaces crude variant presets with a verifiable permission model where every privileged action requires explicit OS entitlement and recorded user consent.
features.howItWorks: Before any tool runs, the engine verifies: Is it within channel ceiling? Does hardware afford it? Has the OS granted permission (e.g. TCC)? Did the owner consent? Is runtime active?
features.limitsAndInvariants: Absence of consent fails safe to DENY. Renamed capabilities are never silently re-granted.

features.name: Dry-Run Action Simulation
features.oneLine: Backend simulation engine previewing file writes, service restarts, and commands before execution.
features.whatItIs: Allows the user or agent to simulate the blast radius and side effects of an action before committing changes to disk or running commands.
features.howItWorks: API endpoints (/api/settings/simulate/*) evaluate proposed actions against safety guardrails, producing an impact report without executing mutations.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Backend implementation exists but lacks a dedicated frontend visualizer card.

features.name: SourcePrep Hybrid RAG Pipeline
features.oneLine: High-precision retrieval combining BM25 sparse search and dense neural embeddings over system manuals.
features.whatItIs: Local knowledge retrieval system indexing ArchWiki, man pages, FreeBSD handbooks, and system administration guides to ground agent recommendations in authoritative technical docs.
features.howItWorks: Queries are parsed and dispatched concurrently to BM25 exact keyword indexes and dense vector embeddings. Results are merged and reranked using reciprocal rank fusion before prompt injection.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Strict licensing compliance: indices only ingest permitted documentation with verified open licenses.

features.name: Monaco Config Editor with Diff Proposals
features.oneLine: Full-featured editor supporting SEARCH/REPLACE diff preview, automatic backups, and rollback.
features.whatItIs: Allows safe inspection and editing of system configuration files (Netplan, Samba, SSH, systemd units) with AI-assisted proposals.
features.howItWorks: Halbert generates SEARCH/REPLACE blocks. The Monaco editor renders a visual side-by-side diff. Applying the change automatically creates a timestamped backup in ~/.config/halbert/backups.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Atomic file writing: failures abort cleanly without leaving partial or corrupted configuration on disk.

features.name: Sherpa-ONNX Voice Pipeline & VoiceHUD
features.oneLine: Low-latency offline voice conversation with streaming speech-to-text and VoiceHUD visualization.
features.gating: Requires local microphone access and installed sherpa-onnx runtime
features.whatItIs: Enables voice-driven interaction with Halbert using local, private neural speech recognition and speech synthesis.
features.howItWorks: Captures raw microphone audio via WebAudio/PortAudio, runs real-time VAD (Voice Activity Detection), transcribes audio with Sherpa-ONNX, and presents live conversational feedback in VoiceHUD.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Push-to-talk by default: continuous ambient listening requires explicit owner opt-in.

features.name: 'One Mind, Many Bodies' Federation
features.oneLine: Pair multiple computers running Halbert into a single unified mind with distributed hardware bodies.
features.whatItIs: Allows a user with multiple machines (e.g. an always-on Mac Studio host and a lightweight laptop) to link them so they share memory and context.
features.howItWorks: Machines discover each other via mDNS or direct IP pairing. The Canonical Host acts as the primary memory store, while satellite bodies proxy tool execution and local sensory reads.
features.limitsAndInvariants: End-to-end authenticated peer pairing: unauthorized devices on the local network cannot execute remote commands.

features.name: Ambient Home Physiology & HA Integration
features.oneLine: Maps smart home rooms, sensors, and Frigate NVR cameras into the host's environmental physiology.
features.gating: Requires configured Home Assistant URL and Long-Lived Access Token
features.whatItIs: Connects Halbert to Home Assistant, allowing the machine to monitor indoor climate, power consumption, occupancy, and physical infrastructure.
features.howItWorks: Syncs Home Assistant entities via WebSocket API into local state caches. Frigate NVR event streams are analyzed to detect meaningful physical environment changes.
features.limitsAndInvariants: Safe home controls: lock and security boundaries require explicit secondary confirmation before toggling.
